accepted.text: Revenue rose every year across the four fiscal years shown, reaching its high in the latest year.
Operating income rose every year across the four fiscal years shown, with its high in the latest year.
Operating margin climbed sharply from the earliest year to a peak in the second-latest year, then eased in the latest year.
Gross margin peaked in the second-latest year and was lower in the latest year, below even the FY2024 level.
Latest-year net margin was 55.60%, just under the prior year's 55.85% and well above FY2024's 48.85%.
Operating cash flow rose every year across the four fiscal years shown, to its high in the latest year.
Latest-year free cash flow was $96.7B on capex of $6.0B, versus $60.9B and $3.2B a year earlier.
Latest-year net income was $120.1B, against $72.9B a year earlier and $29.8B in FY2024.
The evidence gives no cause for the decline in gross and operating margin in the latest year versus the prior year.

rejected.text: It has reached its largest scale and cash generation on record, while its margins have stopped expanding and eased from their peak.
rejected.reason: unsupported: The margin part is shown: operating margin peaked at 62.42% in FY2025 and eased to 60.38%. But 'largest scale and cash generation on record' reaches beyond the FY2023–FY2026 periods the answer shows, so that part is not supported.

rejected.text: Margins slipping from their peak while capital spending grew suggests its incremental economics are less rich than before, which cuts against the idea of unbroken improvement.
rejected.reason: unsupported: The figures show margins pulled back from their FY2025 peak and capex rising, but nothing measures incremental economics, so the conclusion that they are 'less rich' is an interpretation the answer does not state or imply.
